novelty_flags.label: thm:witness-separation and thm:open-neighborhood-separation
novelty_flags.one_line: The refuted maximum-pairwise-variance surrogate is not tied to a specific published estimator or workflow that uses G(r); Hu et al. is a regret-allocation comparator, not a cited source for this surrogate.

novelty_flags.label: prop:binary-reduction
novelty_flags.one_line: The binary minimax-regret treatment-choice benchmark is established prior art and is properly only a reduction check, not a novel result.

soundness_flags.label: Observed-record symbol O and likelihood statements
soundness_flags.one_line: O=(X,A,R,RY) cannot take the declared star value when R=0; define an observed outcome as Y^obs=Y for R=1 and star otherwise before invoking observed-data likelihood ratios.

soundness_flags.label: thm:local-chart-membership; thm:open-neighborhood-separation; def:witness-benchmark
soundness_flags.one_line: q_n is an array while M_eta is defined as laws P_q, and the neighborhood theorem introduces omega, L_omega, r_G(omega), and rescaled r_alt(omega) without definitions; r_G=argmin is also set-valued before uniqueness is proved.

soundness_flags.label: ass:pilot-diverges and ass:pilot-rate
soundness_flags.one_line: m_n/sqrt(n)→infinity already implies m_n→infinity, so ass:pilot-diverges is redundant.

soundness_flags.label: prop:binary-reduction
soundness_flags.one_line: For fixed compact H, binary Gaussian minimax regret is not generally a constant times sqrt(Sigma): scaling gives L_sigma(H)=sigma L_1(H/sigma), so the asserted factor cannot depend only on H.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: Main local-minimax envelope
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The comparison class is restricted to procedures whose pilot-selected annotation rates converge to a deterministic feasible limiting design; sequential, positive-fraction-pilot, and random-limit designs are excluded.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The equality to V* is claimed only for the deterministic-limit prospective annotation class.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: Finite-support annotation experiment
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The outcome model has known fixed finite support and uniformly interior conditional cell probabilities.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The Gaussian experiment, certificate, and attainment claim are conditional on this finite-support interior model.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper develops asymptotic optimality theory for statistical treatment rules in smooth parametric and semiparametric models.
The paper extends asymptotic minimax-regret treatment-rule results to many treatments and discusses computational game-theory methods for finite-sample rules.
The paper studies minimax-regret sample selection in randomized trials with heterogeneous subpopulations and derives optimal schemes under several conditions.
The method minimizes ATE-estimation variance under an annotation budget and gives a feasible two-batch estimator attaining the optimal asymptotic variance.
The paper gives a model-free two-phase maximin sampling criterion that minimizes a scalar efficiency bound or improves every component for multidimensional parameters.
The paper derives a two-wave Gaussian limit experiment and lower/attainment analysis under a unique local optimum and strong-concavity conditions, expressly excluding binary linear-welfare choice.
The article applies minimax regret to choosing between two treatments after observing a finite sample.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Replace the binary proportionality assertion with the valid Blackwell-order comparison in sigma, and state separately the extra conditions needed for strictness or for an explicit scaling formula.

Either attach G(r) to a precise published maximum-pairwise-variance objective with a theorem/page anchor, or recast the witness as a constructive design-geometry result rather than a refutation of a published practice.
Make P_q versus q_n type-consistent, encode the missing outcome explicitly, and define omega-indexed objective/design maps and the rescaling map before the neighborhood theorem.

Add a direct theorem-level contrast with Higbee's smooth strongly-concave limit problem, identifying exactly which finite-menu tie geometry and selective-annotation nuisance step cannot be represented there.

recommended_next_step: Revise the binary reduction and undefined objects, then anchor or reframe the variance-surrogate separation before sending this field-tier angle forward.
